step: Step 2: Strongest alternative attack (A2 affinity vs A1 size-selective)
constitution_articles_applied: Article III — verifier must never trust the claimant (independent A2 model)
Article VIII — certification must attack itself (A2 attacks A1)
Article XVII — every control must have an attempted bypass

physics_finding.csf_turnover_explanation: CSF production (0.3 mL/min × 1440 min = 432 mL/day) / CSF volume (150 mL) = 2.88 turnovers/day
physics_finding.implication: Even with 95% retention per pass, 5% of therapeutic drains each pass. After 2.88 passes/day × 90 days = 259 passes, therapeutic is essentially gone. This is a FUNDAMENTAL PHYSICS CEILING, not a mechanism limitation.

required_kd_for_85pct_retention.interpretation: To achieve 85% retention at 90 days, the affinity matrix needs Kd ≤ 6.27e-10 M (sub-nanomolar). This is achievable for SOME high-affinity antibodies but NOT for all therapeutics and NOT reliably.
required_kd_for_85pct_retention.gap: Typical Kd (1e-08) is 16x weaker than required (6e-10)

verdict.interpretation: A2 DOMINATES A1 (higher retention for all payloads) but A2 STILL FAILS the 85% buyer threshold. The ceiling is PHYSICAL (CSF turnover rate), not mechanism-specific. Neither A1 nor A2 can achieve buyer-grade retention at 90 days.
verdict.branch_verdict: NEGATIVE_CEILING — the strongest alternative (A2) does not rescue the branch. Both A1 and A2 fail the buyer threshold. The ceiling is the CSF turnover rate (~3x/day), which is a fundamental physiological constant that cannot be engineered around.
